ops.title: Gemini/agy prompts beginning with "-" are parsed as flags — fix oracle-first
ops.description:
Adversarial review of the bindings (2026-07-18, refuter-confirmed parity-5/6) found the gemini-family argv shape treats a leading-dash prompt as a flag: plans emit `-p <prompt>`, and empirically `gemini -p --help` shows help instead of treating `--help` as the prompt; `agy` parses `-p` as a boolean alias for `--print`, so the prompt rides as a positional and a leading-dash prompt is eaten. The Rust core is ORACLE-FAITHFUL here — the Python `GeminiFamilyBackend` builds the same argv, so the bug is upstream in the Python package and pinned into the conformance vectors.

Fix discipline (oracle-first, in one PR): change `spawnllm/backends/gemini.py` to a dash-safe delivery (e.g. `--` terminator if the CLIs support it, or positional-after-`--`, verified against both installed CLIs), regenerate the conformance vectors (`uv run python -m tests.conformance.generate`), port the matching change to `rust/spawnllm-core/src/plan/{gemini,antigravity}.rs`, rebuild the wasm blob (`scripts/build_wasm.sh`), and confirm strict conformance + the Go replay stay green. Low urgency: gemini is never auto-selected and claude/codex deliver prompts via stdin, so only explicit gemini/agy runs with dash-leading prompts misbehave.

ops.text: a leading-dash prompt round-trips through gemini and agy in Python, Rust, and Go
vectors regenerated and strict conformance green in all three replays
